target_customer: Young professionals and corporate employees in Gurugram and other Indian cities renting managed co-living rooms; now homeowners and brokers via software
problem: Young professionals in India struggled with the house hunt and with unreliable rented housing quality and services.
business_model: Managed co-living rent with margin on leased properties; later pure software subscription for property management
product_category: Co-living and managed housing, later property management software

founders.name: Sanchal Ranjan
founders.background_notes: Founder and CEO per YC page.

founders.name: Saurabh Kumar
founders.background_notes: Founder per YC page. Other aggregators list a third name for the founding team; not confirmed.

competitors.name: Zolo (Zolostays)
competitors.what: Managed co-living and PG beds across Indian cities
competitors.traction_then: Series A of 5 million dollars in 2017 per a later summary

competitors.name: NestAway
competitors.what: Rental homes and co-living across Indian cities, described as the oldest player

competitors.name: Stanza Living
competitors.what: Student and young professional managed housing, founded 2017
competitors.traction_then: Grew from 100 to over 2000 beds in Delhi NCR within a year per an Outlook Business piece

technical_complexity.rationale: A rental marketplace and operations stack with property management; mostly operational complexity, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Co-living required leasing and fit-out capital, and several larger funded rivals ran the same model, so the product was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded rivals scaled; ZiffyHomes reduced operations during the pandemic and was running two Gurugram properties with 90 to 100 customers in 2021 per Entrackr coverage.

market_need_then: India's urban young workforce faced a fragmented rental market, and co-living was attracting venture funding in 2017 and 2018 per later coverage.

branding.domain_note: Uses ziffyhomes.com; the site says it kept the domain and brand after the co-living business.

identity.visual_style: Magazine-style editorial layout on current site
identity.voice_and_tone: Calm, editorial and understated; frames itself against NoBroker

branding.community_and_virality: Founders describe building India's first physical social network via co-living; no outside evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly invented name, but no press on the brand itself and small scale compared with rivals.

pivots.to: Reduced operations and rebuilt as AI property management software
pivots.why: Pandemic demand collapse per Entrackr and company site; rebuilt product in beta in 2026 per its site

outcome_analysis: ZiffyHomes raised a small Indian seed of about 2 crore rupees in January 2018 and entered co-living against better funded rivals such as Zolo, NestAway and Stanza. The pandemic cut demand, the company says the original co-living business with 15000 plus tenants shut down, and it rebuilt as a software product in 2026. Unit economics were not disclosed, so that factor is an inference from the asset heavy model.
notes: Seed amount of about 313503 dollars is a conversion given in search summaries of the PTI story; investors from the same summaries and not directly opened (YourStory returned 403). Totals on aggregators range from 434K to 21.6M dollars; unverified. Competitor sources are dated April 2019 or later than 2018, roughly 7 months after the Summer 2018 batch for the YourStory piece; the Outlook Business source is undated. The failure factors are my reading; the company itself only says the co-living business shut down during COVID, while a co-founder told Entrackr operations were reduced not shut.
